## Claims
- [source-backed] The two Theorem 5.4 families are stated to be generating sets, each of cardinality \(N=\binom{a+b}{a}\), and minimality means that no proper subfamily generates. [source-6, lines 14-42]
- [proved] If either known \(N\)-element generating family has quotient \(J/\Lambda_+J\cong\mathbb Z^N\), then its image is a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis and the family is minimal.
- [proved] For \(A=\mathbb Z[x]\), \(\deg x=1\), and \(J=(2x,x^2)\), the homogeneous generating family \((2x,x^2)\) is minimal but \(J/A_+J\cong\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z/2\), so minimality does not imply free integral indecomposables.

## Strategy
Put
\[
a=\min(n-r-i,r-j),\qquad b=\min(i,j),\qquad N=\binom{a+b}{a},
\]
and let
\[
\mathcal F_1=\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\},
\quad
\mathcal F_2=\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}.
\]
Here \(i^j\) has \(j\) parts equal to \(i\); zero parts are omitted. Use the known premise that each \(\mathcal F_\ell\) generates \(J\) and has \(N\) elements.

Assume
\[
Q:=J/\Lambda_+J\cong\mathbb Z^N,
\qquad \Lambda=\mathbb Z\oplus\Lambda_+.
\]
For either \(\mathcal F_\ell=(f_1,\ldots,f_N)\), generation gives a surjection
\[
\phi:\mathbb Z^N\twoheadrightarrow Q,\qquad e_k\longmapsto [f_k].
\]
Indeed, if \(j=\sum g_kf_k\), write \(g_k=c_k+g'_k\) with
\(c_k\in\mathbb Z\), \(g'_k\in\Lambda_+\); then
\[
[j]=\sum c_k[f_k].
\]
After choosing \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^N\), \(\phi\) is represented by a surjective
\(N\times N\) integral matrix \(C\). For every prime \(p\), reduction of \(C\)
modulo \(p\) is surjective, so \(\det C\not\equiv0\pmod p\). Hence
\[
\det C=\pm1.
\]
Thus \(C\in\operatorname{GL}_N(\mathbb Z)\), so \([f_1],\ldots,[f_N]\) is a
\(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(Q\). No proper subfamily spans \(Q\), hence no proper
subfamily generates \(J\). This includes \(N=1\): the empty subfamily cannot
generate \(Q\cong\mathbb Z\).

For the converse counterexample, let
\[
A=\mathbb Z[x],\quad A_+=(x),\quad J=(2x,x^2).
\]
The pair \((2x,x^2)\) generates \(J\). It is minimal: \(x^2\notin(2x)\), and
\(2x\notin(x^2)\). Moreover,
\[
A_+J=x(2x,x^2)=(2x^2,x^3).
\]
Degreewise,
\[
J_1=2\mathbb Zx,\qquad J_d=\mathbb Zx^d\ (d\ge2),
\]
while
\[
(A_+J)_1=0,\qquad (A_+J)_2=2\mathbb Zx^2,\qquad
(A_+J)_d=\mathbb Zx^d\ (d\ge3).
\]
Therefore
\[
J/A_+J\cong (2\mathbb Zx)\oplus
(\mathbb Zx^2/2\mathbb Zx^2)
\cong\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z/2.
\]
It has torsion and is not \(\mathbb Z^2\).

## Gaps
This certificate does not establish \(J/\Lambda_+J\cong\mathbb Z^N\) for the Schubert-ideal families; it proves only that this free-quotient statement, together with their known generation, implies minimality.
